added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(0\leq\delta_1\leq\delta_2\leq1\).  Then
\[
 \mathfrak M_{\delta_1}(b,q,\omega)
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\delta_2}(b,q,\omega),\qquad
 \mathcal P_{\delta_1}(b,q,\omega)
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\delta_2}(b,q,\omega),
 \qquad
 \Theta_{I,\delta_1}(b,q,\omega)
 \subseteq\Theta_{I,\delta_2}(b,q,\omega).
\]
Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq[0,1]\) be nonempty and closed, and put
\(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\).  Then
\[
 \bigcup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)
 =\mathfrak M_{\bar\delta}(b,q,\omega),\qquad
 \bigcup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)
 =\mathcal P_{\bar\delta}(b,q,\omega),
\]
and the sharp sensitivity-range identified set is the already closed set
\[
 \Theta_I^{\mathcal D}(b,q,\omega)
 =\bigcup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\Theta_{I,\delta}(b,q,\omega)
 =\Theta_{I,\bar\delta}(b,q,\omega).
\]
Consequently, for every \(C\subseteq[0,+\infty]\),
\[
 \bigl\{\Theta_{I,\delta}(b,q,\omega)\subseteq C
       \text{ for every }\delta\in\mathcal D\bigr\}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Theta_{I,\bar\delta}(b,q,\omega)\subseteq C.
\]

Suppose \(\mathcal P_{\bar\delta}(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\).  Define
\[
 M_+(\delta)=
 \max_{x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)}c_\omega^{\top}x,
 \qquad
 M_-(\delta)=
 \min_{x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)}c_\omega^{\top}x
\]
when the fiber is nonempty, with \(M_+(\delta)=-\infty\) and
\(M_-(\delta)=+\infty\) otherwise.  Then
\[
 \sup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}M_+(\delta)=M_+(\bar\delta),
 \qquad
 \inf_{\delta\in\mathcal D}M_-(\delta)=M_-(\bar\delta).
\]
Thus every compatible ratio is strictly below one uniformly over
\(\mathcal D\) if and only if \(M_+(\bar\delta)<0\), and every compatible
ratio is strictly above one uniformly over \(\mathcal D\) if and only if
\(M_-(\bar\delta)>0\).  The corresponding finite dual certificates are
exactly those in \(\text{thm:common-history-sign-dual}\), evaluated only at
\(\bar\delta\).

Fix a baseline \(\delta_0\in[0,1]\) with
\(\mathcal P_{\delta_0}(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\).  If
\(M_+(\delta_0)<0\), define the below-one opposite-side feasibility set
and sharp priming breakdown point by
\[
 \mathcal B_-(\delta_0)=
 \left\{\delta\in[\delta_0,1]:
 \begin{array}{l}
 \text{there is }x\in\mathbb R_+^{|\overline{\mathcal S}|}\text{ such that}\\
 E_\omega x=d(b,q),\quad F_\delta x\leq0,\quad
 c_\omega^{\top}x\geq0
 \end{array}\right\},
 \qquad
 \delta_-^\star(\delta_0)=
 \begin{cases}
 \min\mathcal B_-(\delta_0),&\mathcal B_-(\delta_0)\neq\varnothing,\\
 +\infty,&\mathcal B_-(\delta_0)=\varnothing.
 \end{cases}
\]
If \(\delta_-^\star(\delta_0)<+\infty\), the minimum is attained,
\(\mathcal B_-(\delta_0)=[\delta_-^\star(\delta_0),1]\), and a minimizing
vector lifts to a law in
\(\mathfrak M_{\delta_-^\star(\delta_0)}(b,q,\omega)\) having a compatible
extended ratio that is not below one.  For every
\(\delta\in[\delta_0,\delta_-^\star(\delta_0))\), there are finite
\(\lambda\) and \(\mu\geq0\) such that
\[
 E_\omega^{\top}\lambda+F_\delta^{\top}\mu\geq c_\omega,
 \qquad d(b,q)^{\top}\lambda<0.
\]
If the breakdown set is empty, the same dual certificate exists for every
\(\delta\in[\delta_0,1]\).

Symmetrically, if \(M_-(\delta_0)>0\), define
\[
 \mathcal B_+(\delta_0)=
 \left\{\delta\in[\delta_0,1]:
 \begin{array}{l}
 \text{there is }x\in\mathbb R_+^{|\overline{\mathcal S}|}\text{ such that}\\
 E_\omega x=d(b,q),\quad F_\delta x\leq0,\quad
 c_\omega^{\top}x\leq0
 \end{array}\right\},
 \qquad
 \delta_+^\star(\delta_0)=
 \begin{cases}
 \min\mathcal B_+(\delta_0),&\mathcal B_+(\delta_0)\neq\varnothing,\\
 +\infty,&\mathcal B_+(\delta_0)=\varnothing.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every finite \(\delta_+^\star(\delta_0)\) is attained,
\(\mathcal B_+(\delta_0)=[\delta_+^\star(\delta_0),1]\), and its minimizing
vector lifts to a compatible law having an extended ratio that is not above
one.  For each
\(\delta\in[\delta_0,\delta_+^\star(\delta_0))\), there are finite
\(\eta\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) such that
\[
 E_\omega^{\top}\eta-F_\delta^{\top}\kappa\leq c_\omega,
 \qquad d(b,q)^{\top}\eta>0,
\]
and, if \(\mathcal B_+(\delta_0)=\varnothing\), this certificate exists for
every \(\delta\in[\delta_0,1]\).  Absent controlled validation,
\(\mathcal D=[0,1]\), so all range, sign, coverage, and breakdown audits are
controlled by the unrestricted endpoint \(\bar\delta=1\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(u,v\in\mathcal V\), define the events
\[
 B_{au}=\{H_1^0=u,R_{1au}=0\},
 \qquad
 D_{auv}=B_{au}\cap
 \{R^{[u]}_{2av}\neq R^{[0]}_{2av}\}.
\]
The event inclusion \(D_{auv}\subseteq B_{au}\) gives
\(P(B_{au})\geq0\).  If
\(P\in\mathfrak M_{\delta_1}(b,q,\omega)\), assumption
\(\text{ass:bounded-noninfecting-exposure-priming}\) gives, separately for
every \((a,u,v)\),
\[
 P(D_{auv})\leq\delta_1P(B_{au})
 \leq\delta_2P(B_{au}).                                    \tag{1}
\]
Every other condition in \(\text{def:full-law-class}\), including the
observed risks \(b\), external margins \(q\), reference mixture \(\omega\),
randomization, positivity, consistency, common exposure histories, the
first-infection map, and placebo reference stability, is unchanged when
\(\delta_1\) is replaced by \(\delta_2\).  Equation (1) therefore proves
\[
 \mathfrak M_{\delta_1}(b,q,\omega)
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\delta_2}(b,q,\omega).               \tag{2}
\]

The same calculation can be made directly in the reduced fiber.  For a
nonnegative type-mass vector \(x\), put
\[
 A_{auv}(x)=\sum_s\mathbf 1\{h_1^0=u,r_{1au}=0\}
 \mathbf 1\{r^{[u]}_{2av}\neq r^{[0]}_{2av}\}x_s,
 \qquad
 B_{au}(x)=\sum_s\mathbf 1\{h_1^0=u,r_{1au}=0\}x_s.
\]
Because \(x_s\geq0\), \(B_{au}(x)\geq0\).  Hence
\[
 A_{auv}(x)\leq\delta_1B_{au}(x)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 A_{auv}(x)\leq\delta_2B_{au}(x).                           \tag{3}
\]
The normalization, trial-risk, external-margin, common-history, and placebo
stability equalities in \(\text{def:reduced-history-polytope}\) do not
depend on \(\delta\).  Applying (3) to every sensitivity inequality proves
\[
 \mathcal P_{\delta_1}(b,q,\omega)
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\delta_2}(b,q,\omega).                \tag{4}
\]
Finally, \(\Psi_\omega(x)\) itself has no \(\delta\)-dependence.  Taking
the union of the same correspondence over the nested domains in (4) yields
\[
 \Theta_{I,\delta_1}(b,q,\omega)
 =\bigcup_{x\in\mathcal P_{\delta_1}(b,q,\omega)}\Psi_\omega(x)
 \subseteq
 \bigcup_{x\in\mathcal P_{\delta_2}(b,q,\omega)}\Psi_\omega(x)
 =\Theta_{I,\delta_2}(b,q,\omega).                          \tag{5}
\]
This proves all three nesting assertions directly from the sensitivity
restriction rather than from an asserted relation to another paper's model
class.

Because \(\mathcal D\) is a nonempty closed subset of the compact interval
\([0,1]\), its supremum belongs to \(\mathcal D\); write it as
\(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\).  Every \(\delta\in\mathcal D\) satisfies
\(\delta\leq\bar\delta\).  Equations (2), (4), and (5) therefore give the
three inclusions from each union into its \(\bar\delta\) member.  The reverse
inclusions hold because \(\bar\delta\in\mathcal D\).  Thus
\[
 \bigcup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\mathfrak M_\delta
 =\mathfrak M_{\bar\delta},\qquad
 \bigcup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\mathcal P_\delta
 =\mathcal P_{\bar\delta},\qquad
 \bigcup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\Theta_{I,\delta}
 =\Theta_{I,\bar\delta}.                                  \tag{6}
\]
Here and below the fixed arguments \((b,q,\omega)\) are suppressed only in
displays where no ambiguity can result.

We next verify that the last set in (6) is closed, so no closure operation
adds values.  If \(\mathcal P_{\bar\delta}=\varnothing\), the set is empty
and hence closed.  Otherwise, \(\mathcal P_{\bar\delta}\) is a closed subset
of the finite probability simplex: all of its equality and inequality maps
are continuous, its coordinates are nonnegative, and their sum is one.
Every sequence in this fiber therefore has a coordinatewise convergent
subsequence, obtained by successively extracting subsequences for its
finitely many coordinates; the limit remains in the fiber by the displayed
closed constraints.  Thus the fiber is sequentially compact.

Write
\(u(x)=\rho_{11}(x,\omega)\) and
\(d(x)=\rho_{21}(x,\omega)\).  These are continuous nonnegative linear
functionals.  If some \(x\) has \(u(x)=d(x)=0\),
\(\text{def:extended-ratio-image}\) gives
\(\Theta_{I,\bar\delta}=[0,+\infty]\), which is closed.  Otherwise, take
any convergent sequence of values in \(\Theta_{I,\bar\delta}\) and choose a
witness \(x_n\) for each value.  Along a subsequence, \(x_n\to x\) in the
fiber.  If \(d(x)>0\), continuity gives convergence to
\(u(x)/d(x)\).  If \(d(x)=0\), the exclusion of a joint zero gives
\(u(x)>0\), and consequently \(u(x_n)/d(x_n)\to+\infty\), with an already
infinite term interpreted by the same extended-ratio rule.  In both cases
the limit belongs to \(\Theta_{I,\bar\delta}\).  Hence this extended image is
closed in \([0,+\infty]\).  Combining this fact with (6) and the updated
definition of \(\Theta_I^{\mathcal D}\) proves
\[
 \Theta_I^{\mathcal D}(b,q,\omega)
 =\Theta_{I,\bar\delta}(b,q,\omega).                         \tag{7}
\]
By \(\text{thm:extended-sharp-identified-set}\), the right side of (7) is
exactly, not merely an outer bound on, the extended ratios generated by
\(\mathfrak M_{\bar\delta}\).  Together with the first equality in (6),
this proves sharpness over the entire sensitivity-range law class, including
the positive-denominator, infinite, and joint-zero branches.  The asserted
coverage-audit equivalence follows immediately from the last equality in
(6): a set contains every pointwise identified set if and only if it contains
their union, which is the \(\bar\delta\) set.

For sign reporting, (4) implies that \(M_+\) is nondecreasing and \(M_-\) is
nonincreasing on nonempty fibers.  The conventions in the statement also
handle empty smaller fibers.  Since \(\bar\delta\in\mathcal D\),
\[
 \sup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}M_+(\delta)=M_+(\bar\delta),
 \qquad
 \inf_{\delta\in\mathcal D}M_-(\delta)=M_-(\bar\delta).     \tag{8}
\]
For every compatible \(x\), the definition of \(c_\omega\) gives
\[
 c_\omega^{\top}x
 =\rho_{11}(x,\omega)-\rho_{21}(x,\omega).                  \tag{9}
\]
Strict negativity in (9) forces a positive denominator and a ratio below
one.  Strict positivity gives either a positive-denominator ratio above one
or the \(+\infty\) branch.  A joint zero has contrast zero and therefore
precludes either strict fiber-wide conclusion.  The pointwise equivalences
and the displayed dual certificates now follow from
\(\text{thm:common-history-sign-dual}\); (8) shows that only its
\(\bar\delta\) instance is needed for a uniform range conclusion.

It remains to prove that the two breakdown definitions are sharp and
attained.  We give the below-one argument first.  For a fixed \(\delta\),
membership in \(\mathcal B_-(\delta_0)\) is feasibility of the explicitly
displayed finite linear system in the variable \(x\).  Nesting (4) shows
that if \(\delta\) belongs to \(\mathcal B_-(\delta_0)\), then every
\(\delta'\in[\delta,1]\) also belongs, using the same witness \(x\).
Thus the breakdown set is an upper set.

It is also closed.  Let \(\delta_n\) be a convergent sequence in
\(\mathcal B_-(\delta_0)\), with limit \(\delta\), and choose corresponding
witnesses \(x_n\).  The witnesses lie in the finite simplex, so the same
coordinatewise subsequence argument used above gives \(x_n\to x\).  The
equalities pass to the limit.  For every \((a,u,v)\), the sensitivity
inequality passes to the limit as
\[
 A_{auv}(x_n)-\delta_nB_{au}(x_n)\leq0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 A_{auv}(x)-\delta B_{au}(x)\leq0,                          \tag{10}
\]
because both mass functionals are linear.  Nonnegativity and
\(c_\omega^{\top}x_n\geq0\) also pass to the limit.  Therefore
\(\delta\in\mathcal B_-(\delta_0)\).  If the set is nonempty, take a
sequence in it decreasing to its infimum.  Closedness puts the limiting
infimum in the set, so the minimum is attained; the upper-set property then
gives
\[
 \mathcal B_-(\delta_0)=[\delta_-^\star(\delta_0),1].        \tag{11}
\]

For \(\delta\in[\delta_0,\delta_-^\star(\delta_0))\), or for every
\(\delta\in[\delta_0,1]\) when the breakdown set is empty, nesting from the
nonempty baseline fiber makes \(\mathcal P_\delta\) nonempty, while failure
of opposite-side feasibility gives
\(c_\omega^{\top}x<0\) for every point in that compact fiber.  The maximum
is therefore strictly negative.  The below-one half of
\(\text{thm:common-history-sign-dual}\) supplies finite
\(\lambda\) and \(\mu\geq0\) satisfying the certificate in the statement.
At a finite threshold, let \(x^\star\) be an attaining witness from (10)--(11).
Theorem \(\text{thm:exact-history-compression}\) lifts \(x^\star\) to a law
in \(\mathfrak M_{\delta_-^\star(\delta_0)}(b,q,\omega)\).  By (9), if its
denominator is positive its ratio is at least one; if the denominator is
zero, nonnegativity and \(c_\omega^{\top}x^\star\geq0\) give either the
\(+\infty\) branch or the joint-zero branch, and each contains a value not
below one.  This is the promised compatible counterlaw at the first feasible
opposite-side value, rather than merely an algebraic failure of a certificate.

For the above-one frontier, replace the final inequality by
\(c_\omega^{\top}x\leq0\).  The limit calculation (10), nesting, closedness,
and the upper-set argument are unchanged and give
\(\mathcal B_+(\delta_0)=[\delta_+^\star(\delta_0),1]\) whenever the set is
nonempty.  Before that threshold the compact nonempty fiber has a strictly
positive minimum, so the above-one half of
\(\text{thm:common-history-sign-dual}\) yields the stated finite
\((\eta,\kappa)\) certificate.  At a finite threshold, exact history
compression lifts an attaining vector.  If its denominator is positive,
(9) gives a ratio at most one; if its denominator is zero, the inequality
\(c_\omega^{\top}x\leq0\) and nonnegativity force a joint zero, whose
extended-ratio branch contains a value not above one.  This proves the
symmetric compatible counterlaw and completes the breakdown characterization.
added_lemmas.justification: The sensitivity classes are ordered by the allowed priming fraction, so the scientifically admissible range has one exact maximal fiber rather than a continuum envelope. The same order defines computable, attained sign-breakdown frontiers.
added_lemmas.gap: Existing pointwise bounds do not by themselves show that a closed sensitivity range collapses exactly to its largest admissible priming value or identify the first priming value admitting an opposite-sign compatible law.
added_lemmas.consumer: Trial analysts solve the identification, strict-sign, and whole-set coverage problem only at \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\), and solve an explicit feasibility problem to report the sharp priming breakdown point with a dual certificate or compatible counterlaw.

proposed_core_edits.name: ThetaIRange

proposed.name: ThetaIRange
proposed.type: subset of the extended nonnegative line
proposed.def: For nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\subseteq[0,1]\), let \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\) and define \(\Theta_I^{\mathcal D}(b,q,\omega)=\Theta_{I,\bar\delta}(b,q,\omega)\).
proposed.role: sensitivity-range sharp identified set, equal to the maximal admissible sensitivity fiber

proposed_core_edits.reason: Sensitivity nesting proves that the union over a nonempty closed range equals the fiber at \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\), and the extended ratio image of that finite compact fiber is already closed. The old closure-of-a-continuum formula is therefore redundant.

The proposition is replaced by the directed, stronger theorem proving law, fiber, and identified-set nesting; exact maximal-fiber collapse; single-endpoint sign and coverage reduction; and attained sharp priming-breakdown frontiers.

prose_updates.tldr: Changing pathogen variants make early-versus-late vaccine challenge risk depend on one latent coupling of exposures and responses across periods. The response type permits a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter later controlled susceptibility, and \(\delta\in[0,1]\) bounds the altered fraction. The compatible full-law classes, reduced fibers, and sharp extended ratio sets are nested in \(\delta\); hence every nonempty closed sensitivity range \(\mathcal D\) equals its single maximal fiber at \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\), without a closure or continuum supremum. Explicit opposite-side feasibility programs yield attained sharp priming-breakdown points, dual sign certificates below each threshold, and compatible counterlaws at each finite threshold. Reciprocal endpoints remain attained under the separate denominator condition. For \(K=2\), the Janvin--Stensrud and Perényi--Stensrud links are projection/calibration comparisons, not model-class inclusions. Exact multinomial inversion with \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\) gives unconditional whole-set coverage, and nesting reduces every prespecified range-coverage audit to \(\bar\delta\). External exposure margins remain primitives and are not replaced by case-strain frequencies.

project_justification.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give sharp single-pathogen challenge-effect bounds, and Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5) identify a variant-specific time-to-event challenge subtype effect under their exposure and proportionality restrictions. Neither supplies the present sharp common-history ratio set from trial first-infection risks plus external variant-exposure margins when a prior noninfecting exposure may alter later controlled susceptibility. Their results also do not establish the sensitivity nesting that collapses an entire closed priming range to its largest admissible value or the attained opposite-sign breakdown frontier derived here. These are projection/calibration comparisons only, not claims of class inclusion or transfer.
project_justification.niche: The target compares one policy-fixed reference mixture across periods and defines period-two challenge risk after no period-one exposure. A history-indexed response array separates that target response from the response after a noninfecting exposure, while \(\delta\) restricts their disagreement without substituting selected case-strain frequencies for external exposure margins. Because the restriction relaxes monotonically in \(\delta\), a scientifically justified nonempty closed range \(\mathcal D\) has the exact least-favorable endpoint \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\). Routine negative tests and serial serology do not justify a small \(\delta\), so analysis without a controlled validation substudy uses \(\bar\delta=1\).
project_justification.fill: The substantive chain gives exact common-history compression, an always-defined extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the disclosed denominator condition, and a common-law sign dual. It further proves direct nesting of the compatible laws, fibers, and sharp sets; exact equality of every closed sensitivity-range model with the single \(\bar\delta\) model; and explicit attained lower- and upper-sign priming-breakdown programs. Below a finite threshold the sign dual certifies robustness, while at the threshold exact history compression supplies a compatible counterlaw. For \(K=2\), finite programs compute the projection/calibration boundary to the Perényi--Stensrud observed contrast; the single-variant inequality is likewise a calibration projection to the Janvin--Stensrud geometry, not a class inclusion. Exact primitive-cell multinomial inversion projects through the maximal nonempty fiber, yielding unconditional whole-set coverage for the entire prespecified range.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The trial and exposure cell probabilities are covered by exact likelihood-ratio-ordered multinomial inversions at Bonferroni level \(\alpha/4\) for each of two arms and two periods. At total count zero, \(T_p(0)=0\) and \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), so zero-total and zero-cell samples require no correction. The simultaneous primitive confidence set is projected through every nonempty candidate fiber. Because \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) is nested in \(\delta\), whole-set coverage over a prespecified nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\) reduces exactly to projection through its largest admissible value \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\); no continuum union or closure is needed. The simultaneous guarantee is unconditional over the trial and external samples, uses no independence among count blocks, and does not studentize or select an endpoint optimizer.

prose_updates.related_work: Janvin and Stensrud (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix B) establish sharp finite single-pathogen two-period challenge-effect bounds and attaining laws. The present \(K=1\), no-priming inequality is a projection/calibration result recovering their survivor-selection geometry; it is not a model-class inclusion or a transfer of their theorem. Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and the marginal \(CSE_k\) identification proposition) identify a time-to-event challenge subtype effect from observed cause-specific hazards under their stated time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, covariate-invariant exposure-ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality conditions. Here their controlled-risk coordinates are projected from \(\rho_{ta}(x,e^{(v)})\), with the period-two coordinate based on \(R^{[0]}_{2av}\); the affine-hull quadratic test and observed-value equality form an exact projection/calibration boundary, not a claim that either paper's model class contains the other. Tomer and Biccler (2022) analyze temporal movement under specified competing-variant mechanisms. Follmann and Huang (2018), Gilbert et al. (2001), Edlefsen (2014), and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) explain why selected infecting strains require extra exposure and susceptibility restrictions, so case frequencies are not substituted for the external margins \(q\). Balke and Pearl (1997) inform the finite response-type lift. Romano and Shaikh (2010) and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) inform whole-set projection; the present exact multinomial construction includes \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), obtains simultaneous unconditional coverage by a union bound without block independence, and uses sensitivity nesting to reduce the full closed-range audit to \(\bar\delta\).
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The parameter \(\delta\) controls whether a period-one exposure that did not infect changes the period-two controlled response relative to no prior exposure. Routine negative tests establish noninfection, not absence of immune priming, and serial serology need not detect response-relevant cellular or mucosal changes; neither identifies a small \(\delta\). Without a randomized or controlled validation substudy, the honest range is \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\), and nesting makes its exact least-favorable endpoint \(\bar\delta=1\). The sharp breakdown point is an identified-law feasibility frontier conditional on the maintained common-history model and external margins, not a validation estimate of the biological priming fraction. The finite map still abstracts from multiple distinct noninfecting exposures within one period.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Exact common-history projection, the unconditional extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the separately disclosed fiber-wide denominator condition, and common-history sign separation hold pointwise in prespecified \(\delta\). The new range theorem proves nesting only within this paper's own sensitivity-indexed class: for nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\), its law union, reduced-fiber union, sharp ratio set, uniform sign audit, and whole-set coverage audit reduce exactly to \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\). It does not assert inclusion in, inclusion of, or theorem transfer from the Janvin--Stensrud or Perényi--Stensrud model classes; those links are projection/calibration results. The target period-two risk uses \(R^{[0]}_{21v}\), while observed period-two infections use \(R^{[H_1]}_{2av}\); their discrepancy among noninfected exposees is bounded rather than suppressed. Each finite sign-breakdown threshold is attained and has a compatible counterlaw, but its scientific relevance is limited by external validation of \(\delta\). For \(K=2\), collapse to the observed hazard contrast additionally requires observed positivity, positive controlled-risk-face feasibility, the affine-hull quadratic identity, and equality of its constant with the observed value. External exposure margins remain primitives; pooled case-strain frequencies do not replace them.

statement_notes.justification: Monotonic relaxation of the priming-fraction restriction makes the largest admissible \(\delta\) an exact, not conservative, representative of the full closed sensitivity range.
statement_notes.gap: Pointwise partial-identification analyses do not automatically prove range collapse, threshold attainment, or compatible counterlaws at the first sign failure.
statement_notes.consumer: Analysts solve one maximal-fiber identification and coverage problem and report an explicit LP-feasibility breakdown frontier with dual certificates below it.
